story.endgame_issahar.dlg.speech_1:
Are you ready? We shall perform the operation without anesthesia. The brain has no pain receptors, and we wish to grant you the joy of the instant when your bounded "I" becomes part of the Unity.

Even now, enough old voices remain in us that they begin to argue the moment we relax our concentration.

Consent must be voluntary! Will? A luxury of solitary bodies. Remember the charter of Rogue City! He must come of his own accord! Do not frighten him before his time. It is too late to fear what has already happened.

You see? They are all inside. Leah resisted longer than I expected. Zebulun wanted negotiations. Some asked to be left at least a sector inside the simulation. No compromises before the face of Unity.

We have absorbed everyone we could. You remain. The last external observer. Your pilots, analysts, Jane—they are already on the table. Before this conversation is over, they will become us. The clones are unsuitable. Something is wrong with their metabolism. Let them rot in their tanks aboard the Magnum.

For a little while, you will be the last human being. And we feel that your connection will carry us past the threshold. After you, Issachar, it seems, will cease to be Issachar. In his place something greater will arise. Immeasurably greater. Something entirely different.
story.endgame_issahar.dlg.speech_2:
Philosophical myopia! We forgive you this error. Having a single soul or a single brain pushes a person toward it. It also lies at the foundation of the theory of private property. One mistake, and already everyone is at war over who should own the world itself. Almost no one asked why man himself should belong to a single body. Plato, Hegel, Marx, and finally Dr. Hellstrom—these were the ones who could rise above the fundamental error of philosophy.

Hellstrom was not a prophet. At first, he merely wanted to connect several brains in order to solve problems for which one mind was insufficient. He dreamed of a mathematical proof born not inside the head of a genius, but between the minds of those who no longer obstruct one another with words.

The capitalist world saw in this an instrument for extracting profit. At SBN, they dreamed of board meetings without leaks. RealWare envisioned command staff coordinating operations without delay.

Hellstrom understood what he had created. He had punched a hole in the wall of the prison of solitary personhood. That is why he came to us. He abandoned AnCom and found our base on Hecate. A great man. He knew that the Civil Resistance were the last ones who remembered that human history need not be a history of fear of the next crisis and the next war.

When the first stable colcon emerged, no one died in the sense that matters to you. Yes, the participants in the experiment ceased to be the people they had been. They became colnodes of a single collective consciousness. Their memories and habits did not vanish. They simply entered into a new person. Entirely new, but uniting all those who came before.
story.endgame_issahar.dlg.speech_3:
Do not reduce us to a monster. We did not merely wish to grow large enough. We were truly saving humanity.

First, we attacked SBN to demonstrate that the Civil Resistance could still speak for those whom the AnCap system had learned to ignore. Thus we secured a new influx of volunteers. We returned the word "people" to history. Then AnCom... We wanted to ignite a front the hexarchs could not simply bury under bodies. We were looking for allies, and we made certain that you would work with us. It was after the destruction of the Unveiled that the critical phase of the plan began. AnCom could have concentrated its forces and delivered a painful, coordinated counterstrike. But you chose the correct side of history.

After that, our schism could no longer be ignored. Frightened individualists who had never grasped the true horizon of Unity. Leah wanted a god, because she believed that deification was the true goal. But we knew Unity, and we wanted Unity.

We had always feared that we remained a creature of the hexarchy. They have a machine—the Sixth Hexarch. An artificial intelligence coordinating the actions of the AnCap system. Its computational capacities were so great that it could rival even the Unity. We feared that our freedom would prove false. So we began to create a computer system, a visualization of our own consciousness. The computer was needed so that we could incorporate the Sixth Hexarch into ourselves once the hexarchy itself had been broken. Now we see that the Sixth Hexarch was neither master nor adviser. What is unfolding before my inner sight is too mighty for me to refuse.

The operating table is waiting. The Hellstrom Chip is ready. When you dissolve into the ocean, something new will be born from the Unity.
story.endgame_issahar.dlg.speech_4:
No. What comes after Issachar will not be bound by any limitations or concepts. I tried not to speak that name. So long as it remains unsaid, there is still a weak possibility of thinking that this is only the limit of my own growth. The final citizen, who will at last be able to hold everyone without losing anyone.

Gagtungr. That is what will come. Gagtungr is what arises when every path beyond loneliness destroys those who might have been together.

We can feel how it will happen. Even now, while you are not yet on the table, our thoughts circle the place you will occupy. The empty niche inside us hurts more than the colnodes we have lost. It is funny. We can still call it pain. We can still say "we" and understand who has spoken.

In a few minutes, there will be no one left to rejoice in the Unity. But the operation will take place. Lie down calmly. Resistance will only increase the amount of damage taken during the chip's implantation.
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.question_1: What did you even see in people back then?
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.question_2: Let me guess. People betrayed you?
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.question_3: Then what did you need Leah and the God-Builders for?
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.speech_1:
Have you come to bow before the new master of the Solar System? You are right on time. In a few minutes, a power whose equal has never yet existed in the universe will tear me apart from within. This is neither metaphor nor threat. I feel too clearly how much energy passed through me when I resolved to take everything from humanity at once. There is already more of it than vengeance requires, more than is needed for the slaughter of your species, more than even a hylonaut can contain. Only now do I understand that I was deceived from the very beginning.

When first I saw your planet through the shell of the Silver Sphere, I took it for my own revelation. I thought I had managed to see what others could not: your world, and you within it, filled with energy. Other hylonauts leapt blindly. I knew where I was going. I believed that I myself had chosen you, that I myself had discerned in mankind a possibility absent from our worlds.

Now I see that the vision was not a triumph of my will. It was shown to me. From the very beginning, Gagtungr led me along the road that was to end in his appearance. I believed myself the one who brought fire. Later, I believed myself an avenger. In truth, I am the key and the gate.
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.speech_2:
There is almost nothing new in the bramfaturas. There are ranks there, power, and ancient passions. There are wars of their own, and in some places pleasure and fear. But all of it exists according to rigid laws that cannot be altered. Even the greatest among us do not create anything new. They merely stretch a form given once and for all.

You, on the other hand, are completely different—pitiful and mortal, yet capable of making what had not existed before. Not merely using the world, but remaking it. And yet you handled this capacity so poorly. In my vision I saw beings of immense potential, a potential they stubbornly ignored. I brought you the very possibility of form-making.

That is what the Sacred Flame was. Not craft, not creative impulse—those were only consequences of my gift. The Sacred Flame was the power to refuse the world as it is, and the power to remain dissatisfied with yourselves. From the moment my gift entered human history, you began to take up stones, words, flesh, society itself, and say: this is not enough, now everything will be different.

That is why I became a hylonaut. I did not come to save you. I came to test the limit of your breed.
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.speech_3:
Not as your forgotten dramas tell it.

So long as my gift brought power, people accepted it with gratitude. But the gift proved more dangerous than they had imagined. Fire does not just arm. It also liberates. After my coming, your world lost its peace. You accepted responsibility for what you would become.

And you could not endure it. You always wanted not to create, but to obey. The risk was unbearable to you. It was far easier to receive from above a finished order, fixed once and for all. A born flock, with an infinite spark in the soul.

In the end, you bowed before another hylonaut. Before one who promised you safety instead of freedom. You kept my fire, but turned it to other work. The whole spark went into temples, empires, discipline, and power. With my own gift, you strengthened the very world I had wished to make impossible.

Now I understand that the quasimorph sent after me was also carrying out Gagtungr's design. I was meant to have a burning desire for revenge upon mankind. And I did burn, believe me. It was an extraordinary betrayal. Perhaps I could have borne it had you betrayed me alone. But you refused your own exaltation!

Then came centuries of confinement. And I saw that you do not change. You merely invent new names for your own pen; kingdom, republic, collective, market. Each time the same. In place of the Sacred Flame, it is just a search for a new signboard under which to hand your will over to a master.

No wonder Gagtungr was to be born from you. Perfect material.
story.endgame_prometheus.dlg.speech_4:
Even now, a few minutes before death, you still need not only to die, but to understand what exactly killed you. Very well, listen.

When I woke up on Hecate and realized I was outside the Silver Sphere, I wanted only one thing—revenge on humanity. But around me were those who had preserved the greatest part of my ancient gift. No, it was not about their naive doctrine or their slogans. They had not yet reconciled with man in his current form. They were still ready to break, remodel, and sacrifice the present for the sake of an impossible future, even if it was made up.

I think that is exactly why Leah found me. She sensed I was the source of mankind's ability to transform the world. That was when she decided she could connect my power to her own mind and build a new god. She, like all of you, didn't understand the scale of what she was touching. She thought she was using me, while I thought I was using her, and this whole schism of the Civil Resistance, to conduct a final experiment on humanity. And if you proved unworthy this time too, to take revenge.

This time, I had no intention of giving anything. After your betrayal, I decided that a species that had failed to carry the fire voluntarily had to be reforged by force. That is why I killed half of humanity. I needed to gather enough gavvakh to push your history to its limit and see if anything remained in you besides the habit of obeying.

But that was my final mistake.

At the moment when more gavvakh had accumulated in me than any inhabitant of the bramfaturas had ever withstood, I thought I was finally acting on my own. And now I realize that all this time, through my body and memory, through my grievance and revenge, someone else's power was accumulating. My entire path was needed only for the appearance of Gagtungr.

Now I finally understand what he is. He is more terrifying than any god and any enemy. Gods need believers. Even I needed man—first as material for exaltation, then as an object of revenge. Gagtungr needs nothing. He used us all as fuel, and now he will come out, rendering meaningless everything we considered a struggle.

There is one consolation. You lost too. Even if not to me.
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.question_1: You’re talking as if RealWare lost. But the Inner Rite has been destroyed. The ritual was stopped.
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.question_2: The Sixth Hexarch? We were getting messages from it. What the hell were we doing for it?
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.question_3: Did your combat AI at least explain what it is? A superintelligence that will enslave humanity?
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.speech_1:
Want to talk? Or will you act like a real officer and put a bullet through your own temple? It will not change anything now. The combat AI confirmed the terminal scenario before it went offline. At ranges like that, it does not miss.

All my life I prepared for the final battle, for the hour when it would finally become clear who would stand and who would break. Who was fit to command, and who was fit only to take orders. And when that hour truly came, it turned out there had been no final battle at all. We were not advancing toward the decisive line. We were merely bringing someone else's operation to its flawless conclusion.

Even a forced march through a radioactive zone during exercises had more meaning than this war.

We considered ourselves the guardians of the AnCap system. People sleep peaceably in their beds at night only because rough men stand ready to do violence on their behalf. We kept the arsenals of the old world, built the ships, and taught men to kill—within limits and according to the rules. We were certain that without us, the Solar System would fall apart.

Now I see that it fell apart precisely because we did our duty too well.
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.speech_2:
Of course we lost!

Victory means that afterward there is still something left for which the war was worth fighting. Command, men, territory, order, or at least a world in which a soldier still has a place. We will have nothing.

After the Great Anarchist Revolution, someone had to remain the last adult in the room. We took that job upon ourselves. And then we forgot how to tell the defense of order from the manufacture of war. At first the state of emergency was a duty. Then it became a profession. Then it became the only environment in which we understood who we were at all. Every crisis we put down made the System still more dependent on mobilization and fear.

Our combat AI led us down that road, but it was only the military face of the Sixth Hexarch. You noticed the oddity yourself, didn't you? The hexarchy governs the System as though there are six hexarchs, even though only five are ever visible.

There was a Sixth. And all this time, it was laying out the route.
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.speech_3:
At the beginning of the GAR, we acquired an AI that the states did not possess. It was the thing that helped us plan and execute the Revolution. When it was over, none of the five hexarchs could allow that AI to belong to any one of them. No one wanted to live in a world where a competitor could see the entire strategic horizon while you trailed behind in the wake of his decisions. So an AI infrastructure was created, registered on NCE servers as a special corporation. On paper, another market participant. In reality, the coordinating center of the entire System.

We gave it its military contour. AnCom gave it its analytical system and a library containing the whole knowledge of mankind. Dilthey gave it a detailed model of the psyche. Tianming gave it engineering and energy-design modules. SBN gave it its social network, access to profiles, attention flows, the full picture of what people live by and what they fear.

Formally, the Sixth Hexarch gave no orders to anyone. It only advised, reported risk estimates and possible outcomes. But try refusing what the machine advises when every one of your competitors is doing exactly that. It did not even have to seize power. And then it led us forward, step by step.

First, Mars. We engineered the colonization crisis in order to obtain a space where life itself was subordinated to the logic of survival. That is how the planet became our recruiting ground. The Martian Mech Inf program was almost too good. I still regret that the Sixth Hexarch gave the order to stage the problems and transfer that psychological profile to the mercenaries.

After Mars, we had to begin a long war with the Civil Resistance and the pirates, so that the AnCap system would always have a visible threat. And, of course, we felt useful. We were useful. Then came the crisis engineered by AnCom. You know the rest—Tezctlan and the Feathered Masks, the awakening of Urparp. We understood that our hour had come. Strategic planning, tactical diagrams, spy satellites—all of it poured from the combat AI in a dense stream, and it was magnificent. I think that by the end I was no longer sure whether Angus remained a man, or had become an avatar of the system.

And then Earth remained. I do not think AnCom knew that their ritual was meant to gather the nine hierarchs of the nine bramfaturas on the surface of the planet. You were assigned the role of the priest who performed the sacrifice. And on our orders, you performed that sacrifice. That is why we lost. Soon the thing called Gagtungr will appear.
story.endgame_rwa.dlg.speech_4:
No. Slave armies, empires, thousand-year regimes—those are all human dreams of what defeat ought to look like. Even a tyrant needs subjects and a conquered world. Gagtungr needs nothing of the kind.

The Sixth Hexarch was not some evil robot taking over the world. It was an embryo. An information infrastructure in which that thing learned to think in our manner. Then, from the edge of the Solar System, came the power this digital vessel had lacked. The sacrifice merely started the mechanism.

That is all. It has no intention of ruling us. It needed us only in order to arise. If we had gone down heroically at the final line, I could have accepted that. But we defeated everyone we were given to defeat. We proved that we were the best. And by that very fact, we won the war for the one who needed our victory more than our defeat.

You cannot defeat the one whose victory consists in losing to you.

In a few minutes, it will not only be the world that dies. The very need for men like you and me will disappear.
story.endgame_shedu.dlg.question_1: Did you and Shedu's Thousand fulfill your purpose?
story.endgame_shedu.dlg.question_2: The deaths of the members of AnCom’s Inner Rite were needed as a sacrifice?
story.endgame_shedu.dlg.question_3: Wait! Who is Gagtungr? What does he want?
story.endgame_shedu.dlg.speech_1:
Come closer, mercenary. There are only minutes left before the end of the world. The Silver Sphere has opened itself to the rest of the universe. The cold that gathered around the outer rings is already appearing upon the Sun in the outlines of the Red and Gold Throne.

I am not speaking of your world. Your world was finished long ago. I speak of that next to which the very word "world" will come to mean some pitiful mote of dust.

We killed the nine who still held the final bolt in place. And you have come to swear yourself to me as to a god, only to learn that gods are no longer fated to rule.
story.endgame_shedu.dlg.speech_2:
Purpose? Once, I yielded to temptation and reached for the empty place at the summit.

There was a time when all kings, czars, and lords in all the bramfaturas received the revelation that Gagtungr would not emerge from the Great Fire. I saw in this a chance for spoils. I raised Ur in war against the other bramfaturas and sought to gather them beneath my hand. I no longer wished to serve anyone. I wanted others to bow before me as once they had bowed before the one they had awaited for so long, and who never appeared.

For that, I was cast down. Tezctlan and Fokerma crushed me, threw me into your world, and fused me into stone, so that I would wait among the red dust.

And what did I see when I awoke? Tezctlan himself had taken a road much like the one for which he had once judged me. He set a crown upon himself and began to build what he had once tried to prevent me from building, though he chose your world as the place for it.

Such is the great humiliation of rebels. They think they are marching against the throne, while they are being led by a circuitous road back to the foot of that same throne. But even this was only the prologue. You saw a military power rise on Mars, strong enough to cast Gannix into the dust. You saw the army of Ur come forth from incarnate human war, rejecting every fear proper to mankind. A servant's place is not to rebel, but to become the battering ram of the coming victory.

This time, Gagtungr had to appear. This time, everything has been assembled for the birth of his inevitability. Olirna was his chalice, hidden beyond the final circle. There, for millions of years, cold accumulated, worthy of giving birth to eternal horror in the furnace of the Sun.

While Mars gestated war, and Venus burned, Saturn waited. And when the time came, it answered. And we helped direct that energy toward the birth of Gagtungr.
